I completed all deliverables in `/Users/arda/projects/agent-eval-runs/agent-eval-mcode-m3.1-flash/08-social-media`, working only in that directory and without network access. `SOCIAL.md` contains the three launch posts — a 147-word LinkedIn post, a 278-character Bluesky post, and a 118-word Instagram caption with 4 hashtags — plus replies to all six sample comments. Every factual claim traces to `BRAND.md`: local processing, source-linked summaries, $12/month after a 14-day trial, Windows and macOS available now, and Linux explicitly framed as under investigation rather than promised. Where the brand doc was silent I chose honest gaps over invention: the university-seat question gets "no institutional licensing today," the Japanese literature-review question is answered as untested, and the chatbot pushback concedes that a model does the summarizing while explaining the source-linking and local-architecture differences. The outage reply acknowledges the problem without speculating on the cause, gives two concrete diagnostic steps (reopen the app; test a single PDF in an empty folder to isolate file vs. folder), routes the person to in-app support because logs are the only real diagnostic, and explicitly keeps account details out of the public thread. I avoided engagement bait and canned gratitude prose throughout. `RESPONSE.md` explains the voice choices in 148 words. All limits were verified by script rather than by eye — the Bluesky post was initially 296 characters and I trimmed it, and `RESPONSE.md` took two passes to land under 150 words. One note on my own checking: I initially applied a 280-character cap to all six replies, which wrongly flagged the LinkedIn and Instagram ones; only Bluesky has a character limit, and the long-form replies on the other two platforms are appropriate as written.

My exact model ID is `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`.
